skill.name: DevOps & Quality
skill.description: DevOps and quality guidance for linting, type checking, Git workflow, CI checks, tests, and secrets handling.
skill.summary: Standardizes DevOps quality practices for Next.js and TypeScript projects.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged Markdown inline code and a documented .env reference in SKILL.md. Review shows these are documentation examples and quality guidance, not executable code or instructions to access secrets. No prompt injection or semantic abuse evidence was found.

static_findings.snippet: - **Rule**: strict type checking is enabled in `tsconfig.json`.
- **Commit Messages**: Semantic commits preferred (e.g., `feat: add chatbot`, `fix: header overflow`
- **GitHub Actions**: Recommended for running `npm run lint` and `npm run build` on every PR.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 9 documents the npm lint command in Markdown inline code. It is not executable code and does not instruct automatic command execution.
Line 10 lists configuration filenames inside Markdown backticks. These are file references, not shell execution syntax in runnable code.
Line 11 references tsconfig.json as documentation for strict type checking. The backticks are Markdown formatting and create no execution path.
Line 15 shows semantic commit message examples. The examples are not commands and do not provide a command injection vector.
Line 19 recommends CI checks for linting and builds in prose. It does not contain executable skill code or dynamic command construction.
Line 25 references a .env filename using Markdown inline code. It is documentation, not shell execution or a request to access the file.
Line 25 advises keeping local .env files out of version control. It does not instruct agents to read, print, or exfiltrate environment contents.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent linting, type checking, CI, and secrets guidance across projects. This skill gives concise standards for quality gates, Git workflows, testing, and environment configuration.
actual_capabilities: Documents ESLint, Next.js, and TypeScript quality expectations.
Recommends feature branch and semantic commit practices.
Outlines CI checks for linting and builds on pull requests.
Identifies Jest unit testing and Playwright E2E testing as preferred tools.
Summarizes local and production secrets handling expectations.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or ready-made workflow files.
Does not define detailed lint rule settings.
Does not provide deployment steps beyond Vercel environment variables.
Mentions future CI work without implementation details.

use_cases.title: Set Quality Baselines
use_cases.description: Create shared expectations for linting, formatting, type checks, and pull request quality gates.

use_cases.title: Plan CI Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Define pull request checks for linting, builds, unit tests, and end-to-end tests.

use_cases.title: Align Testing Scope
use_cases.description: Clarify which project areas need unit tests and which flows need browser coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Quality Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise quality checklist for this Next.js project using the DevOps and Quality skill.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our pull request workflow against the skill and list gaps in branching, commits, linting, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan CI Adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn the skill guidance into a CI adoption plan with required checks, owners, and rollout steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit DevOps Standards Across Repos
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these repositories against the skill and produce a prioritized DevOps quality audit with remediation steps.

output: Require linting and type checks before pull request approval.
Use feature branches and semantic commit messages for clearer history.
Add unit coverage for utility logic and browser tests for authentication flows.

output_examples.input: Help prepare CI requirements for a Next.js app.
output: Run lint and build validation for every pull request.
Add unit test and end-to-end test stages as the project matures.
Block merges when quality checks fail on protected branches.

output_examples.input: Summarize secrets guidance for the team.
output_examples.output: Keep local environment files out of version control. Use managed production environment variables for deployment secrets.

best_practices: Keep linting, type checking, builds, and tests as required pull request checks.
Use feature branches and semantic commit messages for clearer reviews.
Store local secrets outside version control and use platform variables in production.
anti_patterns: Committing local environment files or secrets.
Treating CI as optional for production branches.
Adding tests only after release issues occur.

faq.question: Can this skill run linting for me?
faq.answer: No. It describes standards and commands, but it does not execute tools.

faq.question: Does it include a workflow file?
faq.answer: No. It recommends GitHub Actions checks, but it does not provide a workflow implementation.

faq.question: Which tools does the skill reference?
faq.answer: It references ESLint, TypeScript, GitHub Actions, Jest, Playwright, and Vercel environment variables.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should teams handle secrets?
faq.answer: Keep local environment files uncommitted. Store production secrets in managed environment variables.

faq.question: Can this guidance apply outside Next.js?
faq.answer: Partly. The Git, CI, testing, and secrets principles apply broadly, but some config references are Next.js specific.
